data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Exequiel means 'God will establish.' In the Bible, Exequiel is the name of a prophet who delivers God's messages to the people. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Exequiel usually hope their child will grow to embody god will establish and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: אֶכְסֵקִיאֵל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם אֶכְסֵקִיאֵל נגזר מהשורשים העבריים 'אֶכְסֵק' ו-'אל', ומשמעותו 'אלוהים יקים' או 'האל יעמיד'. השם קשור לנביא יחזקאל, שפעל בתקופת הגלות בבבל. הנביא יחזקאל היה אחד הנביאים הגדולים בישראל, שקיבל מאלוהים את המשימה להנחיל תקווה לעם ישראל בתקופת הסבל והגלות.

in_greek.name: Εξεκιήλ
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Εξεκιήλ προέρχεται από τις εβραϊκές ρίζες 'אֶכְסֵק' και 'אל' και σημαίνει 'ο Θεός θα δυναμώσει' ή 'ο Θεός θα σταθερώσει'. Ο προφήτης Ιεζεκιήλ, από τον οποίο προέρχεται το όνομα, ήταν ένας από τους σημαντικότερους προφήτες του Ισραήλ, που έζησε κατά την εποχή της εξορίας στη Βαβυλώνα.

in_latin.name: Exequiel
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Exequiel derivatur ex radicibus hebraicis 'אֶכְסֵק' et 'אל', significans 'Deus est qui suscitabit' vel 'Deus est qui stabit'. Propheta Ezekiel, a quo nomen venit, fuit unus ex maximis prophetis Israelis, cui Deus commisit ut populo Israel spem infunderet in tempore afflictionis et exsilii.

in_english.name: Exequiel
in_english.meaning: God will strengthen or God will establish
in_english.long_meaning: The name Exequiel originates from the Hebrew roots 'אֶכְסֵק' and 'אל', meaning 'God will strengthen' or 'God will establish'. Derived from the prophet Ezekiel, one of the major prophets in the Old Testament, the name signifies divine empowerment and steadfastness. Historically, Ezekiel prophesied during the Babylonian exile, offering hope and spiritual guidance to the Israelites. The name Exequiel is popular among Christian communities for its biblical significance and the virtues it represents, such as resilience and faith.

data.cultural_impact: The name Exequiel has been carried by many significant figures in history, including Exequiel Guzman, the first president of the Dominican Republic, and Exequiel Antunez de Moncayo, a renowned Argentine composer. Its meaning and origins linking it to establishment and God convey a sense of strength, authority, and divine guidance.
data.spiritual_significance: Exequiel, as a prophet in the Bible, delivered God's messages to His people. This name carries spiritual significance for those named after him, as it signifies a divine calling or purpose in life, being instruments of God's will and guidance. In a broader sense, the name Exequiel is a reminder of the importance of faithfulness and divine obedience.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Exequiel means "God will establish" in Hebrew origin. It symbolizes a strong faith and trust in God, believing that He will establish and fulfill His promises in one's life. Spiritually, it represents a person who stands firm in their beliefs, knowing that God is in control and will guide them through their journey.

biblical_reference.note: The book of Ezekiel is a prophetic book in the Old Testament, written by the prophet Ezekiel during his exile in Babylon.

historical_references.reference: Exequiel was a Jewish priest who served in the temple during the Babylonian captivity. He is best known for his prophecy in Daniel 10:4-9 in which he is visited by an angel who is dispatched from God to bring Daniel a message. The time period for this event is around 538 BCE
historical_references.context: Babylonian captivity, Jewish priest, angelic visitation and prophecy

historical_references.reference: Exequiel is also known as the author of the book of Ezekiel in the Old Testament. The book is believed to have been written around 570-560 BCE during the Jewish exile in Babylon. In the book, God speaks to Exequiel and gives him a vision of the future, including the restoration of Israel and the coming of the Messiah.
historical_references.context: Jewish exile in Babylon, Old Testament author, vision of future and Messiah
